summary: Sun Station is a Nomai satellite in an extremely close orbit around the Sun, designed by Pye and Idaea to trigger a supernova that would power the Ash Twin Project. It ultimately failed to affect the Sun in any meaningful way, leaving the Ash Twin Project without power for 281,042 years.

behavior: Sun Station has been offline in sleep mode for 281,042 years after receiving no user commands for over ten minutes following the Nomai's death.
Sun Station's hull integrity approaches critical levels late in the loop as solar activity rises; emergency doors close.
Sun Station is destroyed approximately 10.5 minutes into the loop when the Sun grows into a Red Giant and engulfs it.
location: Sun Station is in an extremely close and rapid orbit around the Sun.
Sun Station is composed of two huge modules connected by a destroyed passageway.
Sun Station contains many gravity tiles so users can walk instead of free-falling.
Sun Station contains two inactive Nomai Statues, one on the upper floor and one on the lower floor.
Idaea's corpse can be found inside the Sun Station.
The Sun Station warp tower on Ash Twin connects to the Sun Station.
lore: Sun Station was designed to induce a supernova in the Sun to power the Ash Twin Project.
A supernova was the only power source capable of producing enough energy to send information 22 minutes into the past.
Pye proposed building the Sun Station; Idaea firmly opposed it on ethical grounds.
Idaea argued the potential annihilation of an entire star system was too severe a cost regardless of the knowledge to be gained.
Pye agreed she would not support firing the station unless they were all but certain it would not cause destruction.
Idaea and Pye ended up building the Sun Station together despite their continued ethical arguments.
Construction of the Sun Station was the only Nomai project that caused major division and debate among the Nomai.
The ethics debate is recorded behind the Sunless City energy controls and inside the Sun Station itself.
Pye wrote the original mission statement: 'Science compels us to explode the sun.'
Idaea proposed an alternative mission statement: 'Determine if it's possible to prompt the sun to explode.'
A Nomai mural on the station depicts a Nomai holding scales with the Sun on one side and the Eye of the Universe on the other.

The Nomai's intended cycle: Sun Station fires, supernova powers Ash Twin Project, ATP sends Orbital Probe Cannon's launch order 22 minutes back, and the cycle repeats every 22 minutes until a probe finds the Eye.
The Nomai planned to cancel the supernova once the Eye's coordinates were found, by receiving the coordinates 22 minutes before firing the station.
When fired, Sun Station caused only infinitesimal surface-level changes on the Sun, even to the third eye.
Pye concluded that the Sun Station was useless and could never cause the Sun to explode.
Yarrow asked Pye and Idaea to return to Ash Twin and pivot to investigating Spire's newly-spotted Interloper.
All Nomai were killed by the Interloper's Ghost Matter before they could find an alternative power source.
281,042 years later, the Sun reached the end of its natural life cycle and went supernova on its own.
The natural supernova powered the Ash Twin Project automatically, starting the protagonist's time loop.
mechanics: The primary intended way to access Sun Station is via the Sun Station warp tower on Ash Twin.
Information about the Sun Station warp tower is revealed in the Anglerfish Overlook district of the Sunless City on Ember Twin.
The Sun Station warp tower on Ash Twin is exposed exactly 5 minutes into the loop when sand crosses it.
Only the balcony-side door of the Sun Station warp tower is accessible; the bridge-side door is broken.
Inside the warp tower, the player navigates around spiked plants to reach a zero-g elevator leading up to the warp pad.
The warp pad activates once the Sun Station is centered in the platform's viewport.
A secondary access method is manually landing the ship on Sun Station, granting the 'Hotshot' achievement.
Manual landing requires accounting for the Sun's immense gravity and the Sun Station's rapid orbit.
Using the ship is highly recommended over EVA jetpack for manual landing because jetpack thrusters are too weak.
Players can lock onto the entrances, match velocity to 'park' the ship, and then jetpack inside.
Ejecting the cockpit may help exit the ship since artificial gravity behaves oddly near the Sun.
An in-station readout displays the time until Sun Station is destroyed and the time until the Sun goes supernova.
